what: Test and artifact counts measured in a BUILT PUBLIC EXPORT, which is a different tree from the source and carries different numbers.
why_they_differ: export_public.sh excludes the application-gate test and its artifact along with the strategy documents. The gap is the excluded files and nothing else; if it ever differs from the count of files that script drops, something else is being lost on the way out and that is worth knowing.
how_to_check: git clone https://github.com/raj200501/arc-ttt-public && cd arc-ttt-public && python3 -m pytest tests/ -q --collect-only | tail -1
why_this_is_banked: Ten sentences across seven documents stated the public repository's test count as the SOURCE tree's number, because sync_test_counts.py rewrote them automatically and had no notion that some sentences describe a different tree. Every one was wrong in our favour. An outside reviewer found it by cloning the public repo. Copy about the export now has an artifact to reconcile against.
pass_skip_measured_by: python3 -m pytest tests/ -q, run in the built export on 2026-08-25: '306 passed, 6 skipped, 1 warning in 400.20s'
why_pass_and_skip_are_banked_separately: Two documents said '83/312 tests', a mangled leftover of an older '83/83' that a syncer had rewritten by halves. Any repair of that phrase asserts something about how many pass, so the pass and skip counts have to be measured and banked rather than assumed from the collection count. 312 collected is not 312 green.

verified_against_the_live_repository.how: git clone https://github.com/raj200501/arc-ttt-public.git, then a full pytest run inside the clone.
verified_against_the_live_repository.head: dc80f1d528322600d4402cfaf02c9fa7beacd091
verified_against_the_live_repository.replication_note: Measured twice across a FIVE-DAY gap and two containers: 2026-08-25 in the session that built the export, and 2026-08-30 after the container was reclaimed and the toolchain rebuilt from scratch (pytest 9.1.1, torch 2.13.0+cpu, transformers 5.16.1). Same result both times: 306 passed, 6 skipped. A count that survives a toolchain rebuild and five days is a property of the repository, not of the machine that first measured it. An earlier version of this note said both measurements happened the same day; that was the session's memory of the date, not the clock's, and the correction is in CORRECTIONS.md dated 2026-08-30.
verified_against_the_live_repository.why_this_matters: Until now these counts were measured in a scratch export built by our own script, which is the same class of evidence as trusting the script. They are now measured in a cold clone of the repository a reviewer would actually clone, at a named commit.
verified_against_the_live_repository.the_asymmetry_worth_stating: The public repository's OWN copy said 312 all along -- README, paper/DRAFT.md and EVIDENCE.md are all correct, because export_public.sh runs the count inside the exported tree. Only the internal documents describing the export said 333. The published artifact was never wrong; the private copy about it was.
